source.title: The Vanishing Decision Boundary Complexity and the Strong First Component

record.file_problem: Text includes the full paper through its references and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares optimizers and reports both generalization differences and exceptions that qualify optimizer-based claims.
record.gate_note: Tests optimizer effects on generalization (V4). It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected networks, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. The spectral measurements are related to generalization but are not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out optimizer comparisons on CIFAR-10 with VGG19 and ResNet18, bearing on V4 under the reported learning-rate recipes. Its spectral analyses do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase captures the optimizer findings but omits central conclusions. The authors conclude that decision-boundary complexity is transient, predecessor boundaries indicate final generalization, the first principal component becomes dominant, optimizer generalization is associated with feature auto-correlation spectra, and skip connections balance component dominance while using more feature dimensions. They also report improved test performance with annealing and acknowledge spectral-ordering exceptions.
record.recipe_differences: Compares optimizer-dependent test performance and spectral properties in VGG19 and ResNet18; it does not reproduce the original optimizer-comparison benchmark protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning-rate annealing changes non-SGD optimizer generalization. Optimizer comparisons also differ by architecture: VGG19's auto-correlation matrices are often singular, while ResNet18's are full rank.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature auto-correlation spectra correlate with optimizer test performance, with exceptions to simple rank and largest-singular-value orderings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-spectrum properties can track optimizer generalization within an architecture, but no single spectral ordering consistently explains performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Each compared non-SGD optimizer achieves better test performance with learning-rate annealing than without it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate annealing improves the tested optimizers' held-out performance while increasing training accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet18 generalizes better than DLA, which generalizes better than VGG19.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The compared convolutional architectures differ in test performance under annealed SGD.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are reported for the optimizer comparisons in the supplied text. Several comparisons are conveyed through figures without the corresponding numerical test accuracies in the text. The text does not state the dataset for several optimizer comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows identified beyond the extracted optimizer comparisons and the separate convolutional-architecture comparison.

untested.parts: No comparison of random-label memorization with natural-label generalization.
No width sweep or result beyond the interpolation threshold; double descent is discussed through other studies.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or intervention on local connectivity or initialization.

No language benchmarks, systematic tuning-budget comparison, Adam-to-SGD switching, or controlled test isolating decoupled weight decay. The study does not establish equal training performance for every optimizer comparison.
No batch-size comparison; reported batch size is 128.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.

missing.what: ResNet18 optimizer comparison: the caption explicitly reports annealed SGD as best. Add the adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons; numerical accuracies are unavailable in the supplied figure text.

With annealing, AdamW and momentum SGD are explicitly reported to improve further over Adam's 92.6%. Record their comparisons separately. AdamW's improvement is relevant to V4's recovery clause, although this experiment does not isolate weight-decay decoupling.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. All reported image experiments use CIFAR-10. Schedule improvements and spectral exceptions alone do not warrant limits_scope verdicts on V4. Numerical figure annotations are not recoverable from the supplied text, and uncertainty estimates are not reported.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label test performance are not compared.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
The study does not test language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, or decoupled weight decay as a controlled intervention.
Batch size is held at 128; no large-batch comparison.
The paper measures auto-correlation matrix spectra and explained variance, not magnitude-aware sharpness or the tested norm- and margin-based measures.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adadelta and learning-rate annealing; compared optimizer generalization.
rows.baseline: ASGD and Adagrad: both 90.6% test accuracy
rows.note: Text reports the values directly and describes the improvement as significant.
rows.check: Dataset is CIFAR-10. Adadelta's 91.9% exceeds ASGD's 90.6%, opposite the adaptive-versus-SGD prediction for this comparator. Adagrad is itself adaptive and should be separated from ASGD in the baseline. The authors provide no statistical test for the improvement.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam and learning-rate annealing; compared optimizer generalization.
rows.baseline: ASGD and Adagrad: both 90.6% test accuracy
rows.note: This is an adaptive optimizer result; the paper compares it with other optimizers, not a controlled Adam-versus-SGD recipe matching the claim version.
rows.check: Dataset is CIFAR-10. Adam's 92.6% exceeds ASGD's 90.6%, opposite the prediction for this comparator. Separate the adaptive Adagrad baseline from ASGD; this row does not establish Adam's ordering against momentum SGD.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Trained with RAdam and learning-rate annealing; compared optimizer generalization.
rows.note: The text calls RAdam an exception to the rank trend and says its generalization is very good, but does not give the comparison value needed to judge the V4 prediction.
rows.check: Dataset is CIFAR-10. RAdam's 93% alone does not establish its ordering against a corresponding SGD run. Its exception concerns the proposed spectral relationship, not an established exception to V4.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Compared non-SGD optimizers without learning-rate annealing against their annealed counterparts.
rows.baseline: Each non-SGD optimizer's counterpart trained with learning-rate annealing; exact values not stated
rows.value: Every non-SGD optimizer generalizes worse than its counterpart in Figure 4
rows.note: Aggregate statement over the non-SGD optimizers; the paper says annealed runs typically exceed 99.99% training accuracy while unannealed runs do not reach 100%.
rows.check: Dataset is CIFAR-10. Improving each optimizer with annealing does not measure the adaptive-versus-SGD difference or show that tuning closes it. Split the aggregate into optimizer-specific rows if retained.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimizer test accuracy after learning-rate annealing.
rows.baseline: ASGD and Adagrad: both 90.6% test accuracy
rows.value: RMSprop generalization is described as decent despite reducing matrix rank to less than 10% of feature dimension
rows.note: The text gives no test-accuracy number for RMSprop here, and does not provide a direct SGD comparison in this statement.
rows.check: Dataset is CIFAR-10. The qualitative description supplies no RMSprop accuracy or ordering against SGD. The ASGD/Adagrad baseline is imported from another comparison rather than explicitly compared here.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Compared test performance of non-SGD optimizers trained with and without learning-rate annealing.
rows.value: The annealed SGD model beats all non-annealed non-SGD models in generalization
rows.note: The result compares different training schedules and training accuracies, so it does not isolate optimizer choice.
rows.check: Dataset is CIFAR-10. Annealed momentum SGD explicitly beats all default, unannealed non-SGD optimizers. This supports the effect under unequal schedules, rather than demonstrating an incomplete effect. Split the aggregate by optimizer; training accuracies and schedules differ.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimizer-dependent test performance with learning-rate settings including SGD annealing and Adam default parameters.
rows.baseline: SGD-anneal-lr; exact test accuracy not stated
rows.value: Adam is described as inferior to SGD-anneal-lr in generalization
rows.note: The study does not give the numerical test accuracies in the text. The excerpted result addresses a particular VGG19 comparison and does not establish the broader limited-tuning claim.
rows.check: Relink to V4. The explicit statement that default Adam generalizes worse than annealed momentum SGD is relevant evidence in this setting. Dataset is CIFAR-10; no broad benchmark replication is required for relevance.

rows.subject: ResNet18

rows.note: All three compared architectures are convolutional; this does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks as V3 specifies.
rows.check: Dataset is CIFAR-10. The architecture ordering is explicitly reported, but all comparators are convolutional and therefore do not test V3.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, VGG19: cosine-annealed momentum SGD versus default, unannealed adaptive optimizers
relationships.reason: R6 explicitly reports SGD beating every compared unannealed non-SGD optimizer; R7 explicitly reports Adam's inferior generalization. The schedules differ.
relationships.display_finding: The reported advantage for cosine-annealed momentum SGD over unannealed adaptive optimizers remains unverified, with schedules differing.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, VGG19: annealed Adadelta and Adam versus annealed ASGD
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 report 91.9% and 92.6% test accuracy versus ASGD's 90.6%, reversing the predicted ordering for this SGD variant.
relationships.display_finding: Annealed Adadelta and Adam reportedly achieved higher test accuracy than annealed ASGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, ResNet18: optimizer comparison in Figure 8
relationships.reason: Based on text beyond the recorded rows, Figure 8's caption explicitly states that annealed SGD performs best among the compared optimizers; the missing comparison needs a row.
relationships.display_finding: The reported best performance from annealed SGD among the compared optimizers remains unverified.
